```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache=FALSE, echo = TRUE, eval = TRUE, message=FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align='center')

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(purrr)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyr)
```

This challenge explores all matches of Italian soccer Serie A league from 1993 to current year. The dataset is contained in the website [football-data.co.uk](http://www.football-data.co.uk/italym.php). 

### Challenges
1. Think about how to scrape the data from the website, but write no code at this stage.
1. Ask AI to write code to import data by scraping the website. Select only columns Date, HomeTeam, AwayTeam, FTHG (home team goals), FTAG (away team goals)  and filter rows with a valid (not NA) Date. 
1. Using dplyr and tidyr packages (no for loops!), compute statistics for every team (matches, wins, loses, draws, points, points per match). Hint: mutate a column with the outcome of the match (for instance, H = home teams wins, A = away team wins, P = draw). Then group by team and outcome (home and away) and hence spread the outcome. Do this step without the use of AI.
1. Come up with at least 3 data questions on the data at hand. Just write the questions, do not find the answers.


### Data scraping from the website
```{r}
# 1. Season codes
start_years <- 1993:2026
codes <- str_c(
  sprintf("%02d", start_years %% 100),
  sprintf("%02d", (start_years + 1) %% 100)
)

# 2. Files URL
base_url <- "http://www.football-data.co.uk/mmz4281/"
urls <- str_c(base_url, codes, "/I1.csv")

# 3. Function to read and clean one season
read_season <- function(url, code) {
  read_csv(url,
           col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
           show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    select(Date, HomeTeam, AwayTeam, FTHG, FTAG) |>
    filter(!is.na(Date)) |>
    mutate(
      Date = dmy(Date),
      FTHG = as.integer(FTHG),
      FTAG = as.integer(FTAG),
      Season = code
    )
}

# 4. Create the data frame
if (file.exists("serie_a.csv")) {
  serie_a <- read_csv("serie_a.csv")
} else {
  serie_a <- map2(urls, codes, read_season) |> bind_rows()
  write_csv(serie_a, "serie_a.csv")
}
```


### Compute statistics for every team

First of all we want to add a column containing the match's outcome
```{r results='hide'}
serie_a <- serie_a |>
  mutate(result = case_when(
    FTHG > FTAG ~ "H",
    FTHG < FTAG ~ "A",
    FTHG == FTAG ~ "P"
  ))
serie_a
```

We check if there are any NA values
```{r}
sum(is.na(serie_a$Date))
sum(is.na(serie_a$FTHG)) + sum(is.na(serie_a$FTAG))
sum(is.na(serie_a$result)) 
```


#### Matches stats

I will first create two different tables for the team statistics: one for the home games and one for the away games
```{r results='hide'}
# Home games data frame
home_games <- serie_a |>
  group_by(HomeTeam, result) |>
  count() |>
  ungroup() |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = result, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  # Rename columns: if the away team won, it is a loss for the home team
  rename(loss_home = A, win_home = H, draw_home = P)
home_games
```

```{r results='hide'}
# Away games data frame
away_games <- serie_a |>
  group_by(AwayTeam, result) |>
  count() |>
  ungroup() |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = result, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  # Rename columns: if the home team won, it is a loss for the away team
  rename(loss_away = H, win_away = A, draw_away = P)
away_games
```

Now we can join the two tables, obtaining comprehensive statistics for each team.
```{r results='hide'}
# We can use a left_join, since we know that each team always plays both home
# and away.
matches <- left_join(home_games, away_games, by = c("HomeTeam" = "AwayTeam")) |>
  rename(team = HomeTeam)
matches
```

We want to add additional statistics to the data: total wins, losses and draws, total points ever scored, points per game, goals scored, goals conceded, goal difference.

```{r}
matches <- matches |>
  mutate(
    wins = win_home + win_away,
    losses = loss_home + loss_away,
    draws = draw_home + draw_away,
    matches = wins + losses + draws,
    points = wins * 3 + draws,
    points_per_game = points / matches) |>
  select(team, matches, wins, losses, draws, points, points_per_game, everything())
matches
```


Safety checks
```{r}
# Same number of teams in all tables
nrow(home_games)
nrow(away_games)
nrow(matches)

# No missing values after the join
sum(is.na(matches))

# Total matches counted must be twice the number of rows in serie_a
sum(matches$matches) == 2 * nrow(serie_a)

# Every win has a matching loss
sum(matches$wins) == sum(matches$losses)

# Draws are counted by two teams per match
sum(matches$draws) %% 2 == 0
```

#### Goals stats

As before, I have to create two tables: one for home and one for away matches
```{r results='hide'}
# Data frame for goals scored from home teams
home_goals <- serie_a |>
  group_by(HomeTeam) |>
  summarise(
    goals_scored_home = sum(FTHG),
    goals_conceded_home = sum(FTAG))

home_goals
```

```{r results='hide'}
# Data frame for goals scored from away teams
away_goals <- serie_a |>
  group_by(AwayTeam) |>
  summarise(goals_scored_away = sum(FTAG),
            goals_conceded_away = sum(FTHG))
away_goals
```

As before, we now join the two frames
```{r results='hide'}
goals <- left_join(home_goals, away_goals, by = c("HomeTeam" = "AwayTeam")) |>
  rename(team = HomeTeam)
goals
```

We can add additional derived variables: total goals scored and conceded, goal difference
```{r}
goals <- goals |>
  mutate(
    goals_scored = goals_scored_home + goals_scored_away,
    goals_conceded = goals_conceded_home + goals_conceded_away,
    goal_diff = goals_scored - goals_conceded) |>
  select(team, goals_scored, goals_conceded, goal_diff, everything())
goals
```

Safety checks on goals data
```{r}
sum(goals$goals_scored) == sum(goals$goals_conceded)
sum(goals$goals_scored) == sum(serie_a$FTHG) + sum(serie_a$FTAG)
sum(goals$goal_diff) == 0
```

#### Seasons stats

Additionally, I also want to keep the data for all the seasons that a team has played in the 
Serie A.

```{r}
# Season as a factor: the levels fix the chronological order
serie_a <- serie_a |>
  mutate(Season = factor(Season, levels = codes))

# One row per team and season (team seen as home OR away team)
team_seasons <- bind_rows(
  serie_a |> select(team = HomeTeam, season = Season),
  serie_a |> select(team = AwayTeam, season = Season)
) |>
  distinct() |>
  arrange(team, season)

# One row per team: number of seasons and the vector of seasons
seasons_by_team <- team_seasons |>
  group_by(team) |>
  summarise(
    n_seasons = n(),
    seasons = list(as.character(season))
  )
seasons_by_team
```

Safety checks on seasons frame
```{r}
# Seasons per team cannot exceed the number of seasons downloaded
max(seasons_by_team$n_seasons) <= length(codes)

# No missing values in the new columns
sum(is.na(seasons_by_team$n_seasons))

# Each full season should have 18 teams (until 2003/04) or 20 (from 2004/05)
count(team_seasons, season)
```



#### Complete stats

We build the data frame containing all the statistics by joining the matches, goals and seasons frames by the shared key 'team'.
```{r}
stats <- left_join(matches, goals, by = "team") |>
  left_join(seasons_by_team, by = "team") |>
  select(team, matches, wins, losses, draws, points, points_per_game, goals_scored, goals_conceded, goal_diff, everything())
stats
```








### Possible data questions

1 - Which are the teams with the best and worst points per game and goals difference stats?

2 - Which correlation is there, if any, between goals difference and total scored points?

3 - Which are the teams that scored more points while playing away?

4 - Which team has the best defense? Which has the best offense?

5 - Which teams have been missing from Serie A the longest?

6 - Which teams have consecutively been in the league for longer?

7 - Which teams have the best points per season average?
